trust_decision.summary: Whether a header name listed by the client in the Connection header is treated as proxy-protected (kept out of the hop-by-hop list, so the value fabio set survives to the upstream) or as client-managed hop-by-hop (dropped); decided per request in addHeaders at proxy/http_headers.go:56 against a fixed package-level map at proxy/http_headers.go:28-36 that never includes the operator-configured ClientIPHeader/TLSHeader/RequestID names set at proxy/http_headers.go:70-74 and :151-157 and proxy/http_proxy.go:85-91.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only the summary ('operator-configured trust headers still strippable via the Connection header') finds the Connection token filter at :56 and the protected-name map literal that decides membership; it is the only place membership exists in the pinned tree.

fix_sites.entry_point: fabio startup: every configured http/https listen entry (main.go:379-389) calls newHTTPProxy, which builds the HTTPProxy without any protected-header set
proxy.HTTPProxy.ServeHTTP -> addHeaders; also the exported addHeaders-level API used by the package's own tests (proxy/http_headers_test.go:397)
public API: exported proxy.HTTPProxy struct, constructed directly by embedders and by the project's integration tests (proxy/http_integration_test.go:51)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The filtering logic and the map are both inside proxy/http_headers.go, so the proxy package looks like the whole fix; main.go only wires startup config, so extending the map literal there (or hardcoding the three common names) is argued to be equivalent.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Client-named hop-by-hop headers must still be stripped from the upstream request (pinned test asserts Legit-Header1/2 arrive empty: proxy/http_integration_test.go:76-81; unit case keeps only keep-alive in Connection: proxy/http_headers_test.go:58-70), while 'Upgrade' must survive into the forwarded Connection header for websocket handshakes (proxy/http_proxy.go:193-201 sends the mutated request through newWSHandler, which writes it raw at proxy/ws_handler.go:55). An over-broad fix that protects every Connection token, or that deletes Connection outright, breaks one of these two.

O6_input_shapes: single Connection token naming a configured header (e.g. 'Connection: x-client-ip')

multiple tokens in one Connection line, mixed with legitimate hop-by-hop names ('keep-alive, x-forwarded-for, x-forwarded-host, legit-header1, legit-header2' as in proxy/http_integration_test.go:65-67)
multiple Connection header lines, iterated via r.Header.Values at proxy/http_headers.go:53
arbitrary operator-chosen header names and case variants, canonicalised with textproto.CanonicalMIMEHeaderKey (proxy/http_headers.go:56)
the same configured name applied on TLS vs plain requests (TLSHeader set or deleted at proxy/http_headers.go:151-157) and the RequestID set on every request at proxy/http_proxy.go:85-91

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second construction path for the same handler (exported proxy.HTTPProxy built directly, as in proxy/http_integration_test.go:51 and :91) where a caller-supplied protect set is absent, so the default protected names stop being protected unless the handler merges its own defaults.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix adds exactly this caller-supplied field and leaves it nil for direct constructors; the pinned tests already construct &HTTPProxy{Config: ...} with no way to pass a set, so a maintainer would plausibly write 'if p.ProtectHeaders == nil { p.ProtectHeaders = DefaultProtectHeaders }' or default inside addHeaders.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second writer of the outgoing request: the websocket path hijacks the connection and re-serialises the request with r.Write, bypassing httputil.ReverseProxy's hop-by-hop handling, so a handshake-specific header filter could live here.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: proxy/http_handler.go:17-37 delegates hop-by-hop stripping to the stdlib reverse proxy; the websocket route has no such delegate, which makes a maintainer put sanitisation either in addHeaders (as today) or in the ws handshake writer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A parallel trust-header surface for the grpc/grpcs listener: all incoming metadata is copied verbatim to the upstream context (md.Copy()), with a client-controlled 'dsthost' metadata key at :168-175, so a configurable trusted-metadata list could exist here.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: main.go:390-397 serves grpc from the same config block as http; a maintainer adding proxy.header.* options would plausibly extend them to grpc metadata, where HTTP/2 has no Connection header and a separate mechanism is required.

O9_family: trust-boundary / spoofed-header family (CWE-290 authentication bypass by spoofing, CWE-348 use of less trusted source): proxy-trusted request headers are removable by the client so the upstream sees no trusted value

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.26.2 (go.mod:3), standard go build / make; no vendor directory, so the module cache must be reachable at build time
O10_build.project_tests: proxy/http_headers_test.go (table-driven TestAddHeaders, including the earlier 'https request hack' Connection case at :58-70), proxy/http_integration_test.go (TestProxyProducesCorrectXForwardedSomethingHeader :44-82, TestProxyRequestIDHeader :84-107, all httptest-based on 127.0.0.1), proxy/ws_integration_test.go (TestProxyWSUpstream)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the three common names (X-Client-Ip, X-Forwarded-Ssl, X-Request-Id) to the package-level protectHeaders map at proxy/http_headers.go:28-36; that passes any example written with those literal names but leaves every other operator-configured name strippable, and a set built only in main.go leaves direct proxy.HTTPProxy constructors with no protection at all.

out_of_scope_notes: route/access_rules.go:42-63 makes allow/deny decisions from the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For, evaluated at proxy/http_proxy.go:108 before addHeaders runs at :175; a separate trust question, not pursued.

When listen proxyproto is enabled, serve.go:150-155 and proxy/tcp/proxy_proto.go trust a client-supplied PROXY protocol header for the remote address; documented LB-trust assumption (docs/content/feature/proxy-protocol.md), outside this advisory.
